neighbours.label: existential ' there' opening a 'there is/are' clause after a connective or adverb ('so there is', 'currently there is'), against locative 'there'
fire: The vaccine trial is still small, so there is no firm evidence yet.
At the moment there are only two nurses on the night shift.
The ward was renovated last year, and now there is room for ten more beds.
Because the river froze early, there was no way to bring in supplies.
Sadly, there is no treatment that reverses the damage once it starts.
The shop closed in May, so there are few places left to buy bread in town.
Today there is a strong wind warning for the whole coast.
Since the bridge was repaired, there have been fewer accidents on that road.
quiet: The vaccine trial is run in a clinic, and the nurses work there every day.
At the moment we are driving there with the two nurses from the night shift.
The ward was renovated last year, and patients now sleep there more comfortably.
Because the river froze early, we walked there across the ice.
Sadly, we never went back there after the old house was sold.
The shop closed in May, so nobody goes there to buy bread anymore.
Today we hiked up to the lighthouse and had lunch there.
Since the bridge was repaired, I cycle there every morning.

notes: Card: ' there' x19, all 'so/currently/as/that there is'. Probe: currently there is 0.539, so there is plenty 0.437, so there is little 0.270; stayed there 0.024, over there 0.013, 'There, there' 0.022. Other subjects also fire at that slot ('Currently it is' 0.283, 'until control is' 0.250), so near misses keep 'there' and drop the existential use.
